text:
maria_ops: Heads-up: APAC cooling capacity at AKL rack 7 has degraded due to sustained heatwave. After consulting facilities, we need to run a staggered cooldown and node-drain to avoid thermal throttling. Planning window: Tue 2026-07-21 01:00-05:00 UTC (local evening). Expected impact: up to ~12% GPU capacity reduction in apac1 during the window.

maria_ops: Goal is zero-P99 latency regression for hosted customers. We'll route traffic off draining nodes using existing routing policies and enable temporary burst on dedicated pools where contracts allow. Private deployments not affected.

ashley_sre: Thanks — are we doing full reboots or soft kernel-level offlines? I want the runbook so oncall can watch GPUs for temp spikes.

maria_ops: Soft drains + controlled cool-off then reboot if temperatures still >70C. We'll run `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force <node>` and follow the thermal-check script. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/apac-heatwave-cooldown (see checklist).

ashley_sre: Copy. Can you paste the thermal-check command we run?

maria_ops: Thermal check snippet: ```bash
# check GPU temps and fan speeds
ssh node-01 "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,fan.speed --format=csv,noheader"
if [ "$TEMP" -gt 68 ]; then sleep 300; fi
```

tj_infra: A couple questions: 1) How aggressive is our routing fallback to eu/us? We risk added egress and inter-region latency. 2) Cost impact if we burst on dedicated pools — need an estimate to flag finance.

maria_ops: Good Qs. 1) Default policy: latency-priority routes remain but any node marked DRAIN will be deprioritized; model variants in eu/us will be preferred for non-SLA customers. We will not failover customer-pinned model versions unless they opt-in. 2) Estimate: short burst (up to 3h) ~+$6k across peak window (rough guesstimate); I'll hand off a calc after we finalize the node list.

devex_kevin: Should we send a customer advisory? I'd rather notify teams who have pinned versions in apac to avoid surprises. Can we include mitigation steps for customers (pin fallback to regional variants)?

product_zoe: Yes, please. Also add a line: "No disruption for Dedicated Reserved contracts unless specified in outreach." We need legal to sign off on notices for enterprise customers with strict locality requirements.

maria_ops: Will draft advisory and tag enterprise list. Draft snippet: "Planned thermal maintenance in apac1 on Tue 2026-07-21 01:00-05:00 UTC. We expect reduced GPU capacity and potential slowdowns for apac-hosted workloads. No change to private deployments. We recommend customers use multi-region routing or pin a compatible EU/US variant for critical paths."

ashley_sre: Runbook link again for oncall: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/apac-heatwave-cooldown (steps: pre-check, cordon+drain, cool-wait, reboot-if-needed, post-verify). I'll coordinate oncall coverage 00:30-06:00 UTC.

tj_infra: Please include an ops-safe list of node hostnames to drain so provisioning can pre-warm spare nodes. Also note: avoid draining >25% of a rack at once due to power/cooling balancing.

maria_ops: Agreed — we'll stagger by rack and by 15-min offsets. Initial drain list (partial): node-apac1-r07-n[01-08]. Full plan attached to the runbook doc.

tj_infra: Also flagging possible increased spot preemption for burst capacity. We'll prefer reserved pools where possible.

deploy-bot: Maintenance ticket created: MNT-2026-APAC-COOLING-1 | Window: 2026-07-21 01:00-05:00 UTC | Owner: maria_ops | Affected: apac1 GPU pool | Notifying: infra-oncall, product, devex.

ops_announce_bot: Internal notice sent to #general and #customers with advisory link; external customer email scheduled for Tue 2026-07-14 16:00 UTC.

devex_kevin: I'll prepare a short playbook for customers: how to switch routing, pin a fallback, and check usage limits.

product_zoe: Also add a bullet: "We will run smoke tests after each rack cooldown — if regressions detected, rollback policy: route back to eu/us variant automatically."

ashley_sre: One more: telemetry — please tag all drained nodes with `maintenance=apac-heatwave-jul21` so we can slice metrics easily.

maria_ops: Done. Tagging will be automatic as part of the drain workflow. Final ask: volunteers for 01:00-04:00 UTC watch? (reaction :eyes:)

tj_infra: I'm in for the first two hours.

ashley_sre: I'll take escalation 03:00-05:00 UTC.

devex_kevin: I'll run customer comms and be on call for routing questions.

maria_ops: Thanks team. Will post final node list + exact stagger offsets by EOD (2026-07-20 23:59 UTC).
